title: Jira vs Plane
comparison_markdown:
# Jira vs Plane

## Overview

Jira is the industry-standard issue and project tracking tool from Atlassian used for agile software development. Plane is a modern open-source alternative with a clean, fast interface.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Jira charges $7.75-$14.50/user/month; Plane is free to self-host
- **Complexity**: Jira is notoriously complex and slow; Plane is designed to be fast
- **Customization**: Jira has extensive workflow customization; Plane is simpler but improving
- **Integrations**: Jira integrates with the entire Atlassian ecosystem; Plane offers REST API access
- **Performance**: Plane modern architecture delivers significantly faster page loads

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Jira | Plane |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $7.75-$14.50/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$388/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$1,550/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Jira

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Plane

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [makeplane/plane](https://github.com/makeplane/plane) * ~31k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Jira if:** Jira suits large enterprises invested in the Atlassian ecosystem or teams needing highly customized workflow automation.

**Choose Plane if:** Plane is ideal for startups and small-to-mid teams tired of Jira complexity.

## Migration Path

Export Jira issues as CSV, then import into Plane using the CSV importer. Custom fields and automations will need to be recreated.

## Our Take

Plane is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Jira tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Plane instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Jira, switching to self-hosted Plane will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Jira until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Jira paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Plane free to use?
Yes. Plane is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Jira to Plane?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Jira data, follow the Plane import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Plane get regular updates?
Yes. Plane has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Plane without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Plane development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Jira](https://atlassian.com/jira) and [Plane](https://plane.so) before making decisions.*
meta_description: Plane is a free, self-hosted alternative to Jira. Compare pricing, features, and migration steps. See full comparison.

title: Trello vs WeKan
comparison_markdown:
# Trello vs WeKan (2026)

## Overview
Trello and WeKan are two popular project management tools used for organizing and tracking tasks. This comparison is beneficial for teams and individuals who are looking for a tool to manage their projects and want to decide between a proprietary, cloud-based solution (Trello) and a self-hosted, open-source alternative (WeKan). The core use case for both tools is task management, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Trello offers a free plan with limited features, while WeKan is completely free as it is self-hosted.
* Data ownership: WeKan allows users to have full control over their data, while Trello stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: WeKan requires more technical expertise to set up, while Trello is easy to get started with.
* Scalability: Trello is more scalable and can handle large teams, while WeKan's scalability depends on the server it is hosted on.
* Integration with Google Drive: Trello has a built-in integration with Google Drive, while WeKan does not have a native integration.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Trello | WeKan |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $5+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $250/month (assuming $5/user/month) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1000/month (assuming $5/user/month) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Trello:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Scalable and reliable
* Integrates with many third-party apps
* Offers a free plan with limited features
* Limited control over data
**WeKan:**
* Self-hosted and open-source
* Full control over data
* Customizable and extensible
* Free to use
* Requires technical expertise to set up and maintain
* Limited scalability and reliability compared to Trello

## When to Choose Each
Trello is a good choice for teams that need a easy-to-use, scalable, and reliable project management tool. It is suitable for large teams and enterprises that require integration with other tools and services. WeKan, on the other hand, is a good choice for teams that value data ownership and control, and are comfortable with self-hosting and maintaining their own server. It is suitable for small to medium-sized teams that require a customizable and extensible project management tool.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Trello boards as JSON files using the Trello API or a third-party tool.
2. Set up a WeKan server and create a new board.
3. Use the WeKan import tool to import your Trello boards into WeKan.
4. Configure your WeKan board to match your Trello workflow.
5. Test and verify that all your data has been imported correctly.

## Our Take
WeKan is not yet production-ready for most users, as it requires technical expertise to set up and maintain. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that WeKan's scalability and reliability depend on the server it is hosted on. However, for teams that value data ownership and control, and are comfortable with self-hosting and maintaining their own server, WeKan is a good alternative to Trello.

WeKan's technical limitations make it less suitable for large teams and enterprises that require a scalable and reliable project management tool. However, for small to medium-sized teams that require a customizable and extensible project management tool, WeKan is a good choice.

For teams that are currently using Trello and are looking for a more customizable and extensible alternative, WeKan is a good option. However, teams that require a easy-to-use, scalable, and reliable project management tool should stick with Trello.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) that value data ownership and control
* Teams that require a customizable and extensible project management tool
* Teams that do not need integration with other tools and services
* Teams that are comfortable with self-hosting and maintaining their own server
* Teams that have limited budget and cannot afford Trello's per-user fees

## FAQ
### Can I use WeKan for free?
Yes, WeKan is completely free to use as it is self-hosted. However, you will need to pay for the server costs.
### Is WeKan as scalable as Trello?
No, WeKan's scalability depends on the server it is hosted on, while Trello is more scalable and reliable.
### Can I integrate WeKan with Google Drive?
Not yet, WeKan does not have a native integration with Google Drive. However, you can use third-party tools to integrate WeKan with Google Drive.
### Is WeKan easy to use?
No, WeKan requires technical expertise to set up and maintain, while Trello is easy to use and set up.
### Can I import my Trello boards into WeKan?
Yes, you can import your Trello boards into WeKan using the WeKan import tool.

title: Google Workspace vs Nextcloud
comparison_markdown:
# Google Workspace vs Nextcloud

## Overview

Google suite of cloud productivity tools including Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Meet, and Calendar. is a popular proprietary tool in the productivity space. Nextcloud is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Google Workspace costs $6-$18/user/month; Nextcloud is Free (self-hosted)
- **License**: Google Workspace is Proprietary; Nextcloud is AGPL 3.0
- **Data ownership**: Nextcloud can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Nextcloud eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Nextcloud has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Google Workspace | Nextcloud |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $6-$18/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$300/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$1,200/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Google Workspace

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Nextcloud

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [nextcloud/server](https://github.com/nextcloud/server) * ~27k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Google Workspace if:** Google Workspace is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Nextcloud if:** Nextcloud is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Google Workspace in its standard export format, review Nextcloud import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Nextcloud is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Google Workspace tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Nextcloud instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Google Workspace, switching to self-hosted Nextcloud will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Google Workspace until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Google Workspace paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Nextcloud free to use?
Yes. Nextcloud is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Google Workspace to Nextcloud?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Google Workspace data, follow the Nextcloud import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Nextcloud get regular updates?
Yes. Nextcloud has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Nextcloud without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Nextcloud development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Google Workspace](https://workspace.google.com) and [Nextcloud](https://nextcloud.com) before making decisions.*
